questions.question: Where does the orient note live in the trace? The schema has additionalProperties: false at the top level, so a new key means a schema change.

options.label: New `orient:` key (Recommended)
options.description: Add an optional top-level `orient:` list to _schema.yml: one entry per cluster with `items`, `verdict` (enum subsumes/constrains/unrelated), `evidence`, and `read` (the dossiers/RFCs actually opened). check_traces validates it, and run B's check becomes a lookup instead of a prose reading. Costs a schema edit plus its example.

options.label: Orient phase steps only
options.description: No schema change. Each dossier/RFC read is a step in the `orient` phase, and the verdict plus evidence go in its `extract`. Cheaper, but the verdict is free text an aggregator can't count, and run B's check is a reading.

questions.question: When orientation finds no cluster that subsumes or constrains the item, does /ship still ask the scope question?

options.label: One line, no dialog (Recommended)
options.description: Write the orient note, state 'nothing related changes the scope' in one line, and go to plan mode. Plan approval already gates scope. The dialog only fires when it carries a real recommendation to change scope.

options.label: Always ask
options.description: Always one AskUserQuestion with the recommended scope, even when it is 'as framed'. Literal reading of the kickoff; one extra dialog per delivery, mostly rubber-stamps.
